samples.summary: Materializing `lineAffinity: 'backward'` on every caret position leaks into keyboard-built selection *anchors*, silently overriding the documented asymmetric start default
samples.evidence: The approach in docs/tasks/active/20260822-caret-line-affinity-todo.md:29 says a caret position "always states its reading (materialized, defaulting to 'backward')" while "absent stays reserved for endpoints from other producers … which keep computeSelectionRects' asymmetric default". But selection anchors are built *from the caret*: text-editor.ts:2774 (`const anchor = this.selection.range?.anchor ?? pos`), :2807 and :2826 (`?? this.cursor.position`). Previously `cursor.position` carried no affinity, so `buildRects` applied `start.lineAffinity ?? 'forward'` (packages/docs/src/view/selection.ts:260) — the default that exists specifically so a highlight does not open on a zero-width sliver of the line above (docs/design/docs/docs-local-caret-anchoring.md:82-88). After this change those anchors arrive with an explicit `'backward'`, so a shift-selection whose normalized *start* is the caret at a wrap boundary now resolves the start with the backward reading instead of the forward one. Neither the new design-doc paragraph nor any test records this behavioural consequence of the 'always materialize' decision.

samples.summary: Design doc still carries stale rows asserting peer carets default to `'backward'` with an "acceptable minor visual offset"
samples.evidence: The edge-case table (line 516) and the risk table (line 582) still read "Line-wrap affinity inaccuracy for remote cursors | Default to 'backward'; minor visual offset acceptable [for peer display]", which is exactly the statement the body text at :188-198 was rewritten to retract. The repo files docs by validity (fold into the canonical subsystem doc), so leaving contradicting rows in the same file is the kind of staleness this change set out to remove from types/users.ts.

samples.summary: `resolvePositionPixel`'s affinity parameter is not actually optional, contradicting its own doc comment and the stated approach
samples.evidence: The doc comment added at peer-cursor.ts:95-98 says "Omit it to use the affinity the position itself carries", and the task step (docs/tasks/active/20260822-caret-line-affinity-todo.md:41-42) says "affinity param optional". The signature is `lineAffinity: 'forward' | 'backward' | undefined` in a required positional slot followed by four more params, so a caller cannot omit it — it must pass a literal `undefined` (as editor.ts:1570 / :2823 do via `pos.lineAffinity`). A trailing-optional or options-object shape would match the documented intent; as written, a future call site still has to type *something* at the very slot the fallback was meant to make forgettable.

verdict.reason: The code exists as described (cursor.ts:26,52-56 materializes lineAffinity; text-editor.ts:2774/2807/2826 build anchors from the caret; selection.ts:260-261 holds the asymmetric default), but the design-fit allegation does not hold. The design doc explicitly records this exact consequence: docs/design/docs/docs-local-caret-anchoring.md:89-101 says the caret affinity "travels with the position into presence, undo history, selection endpoints and rendering" and that "A caret always materializes its reading ('backward' unless told otherwise); absent stays reserved for endpoints from other producers ... which keep the asymmetric default above", with :103-109 covering DocRange endpoints. That is the opposite of "silently overriding" an undocumented default, and it matches the approach stated in the task file (20260822-caret-line-affinity-todo.md:28-31). The repo's own rationale for the forward start default also contradicts the claimed harm: 20260822-selection-line-affinity-todo.md:18-26 records that a backward-affinity start on a boundary "always produces a zero-width first rect ... so switching to forward only removes an invisible rect" — i.e. the difference is an invisible rect, not a highlight opening on a visible sliver. None of the originating task's acceptance criteria (:55-61) concern keyboard selection anchors, no existing module is duplicated, and no Non-Goal (docs-local-caret-anchoring.md:57-63) is exceeded. The residue — whether backward is the right visual reading for a selection start, and the absence of a test pinning it — belongs to the correctness and test-adequacy lenses, not design-fit.
